examples.japanese: {目|め}が{悪|わる}いので、めがねをかけています。
examples.english: I wear glasses because I have poor eyesight.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{目|め}をした{猫|ねこ}がいます。
examples.english: There is a cat with red eyes.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{時間|じかん}パソコンを{見|み}ていたので、{目|め}が{疲|つか}れました。
examples.english: I was looking at the computer for a long time, so my eyes got tired.

notes:
{目|め} is one of the most common body part words, appearing in many expressions and compounds.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {目|め}が{悪|わる}い: to have poor eyesight
- {目|め}が{覚|さ}める: to wake up
- {目|め}が{疲|つか}れる: eyes get tired
- {目|め}を{閉|と}じる: to close one's eyes
- {目|め}に{見|み}える: visible
- {目|め}を{引|ひ}く: eye-catching

COMPOUNDS:
- めがね: glasses (eye + metal)
- {目薬|めぐすり}: eye drops
- {目覚|めざ}まし{時計|どけい}: alarm clock

COUNTER SUFFIX:
〜{目|め} also serves as an ordinal suffix: {一|ひと}つ{目|め} (first), {二|ふた}つ{目|め} (second).
